example: I'm exhausted, so I'm going to hit the sack early tonight.
origin: Often linked to the sacks or bags used as beds, but the exact origin is uncertain

wrong_meanings.meaning: to hit a bag with your hand
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal reading of the words, not the idiomatic meaning

wrong_meanings.meaning: to be dismissed from a job
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This describes losing work, which the idiom does not refer to at all

wrong_meanings.meaning: to win a game or competition
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: Winning has no connection to going to bed, so this meaning is clearly wrong

explanation: 'Hit the sack' is an informal way to say that someone is going to bed. It is common in everyday speech, especially when talking about the end of the day.
